label: What Strategy Is (and Is Not)
summary: Whether the thing on the table is actually a strategy: an integrated set of choices about where to compete and how to win, aimed at compelling a specific customer action - as opposed to a plan, a budget, a vision, or a list of initiatives.
assess_focus: Classify the artefact before critiquing it. Most weak strategies fail here, and no amount of downstream polish fixes a category error.

label: The Practitioner
summary: Who is doing this strategy work, what they are actually able to decide, and whether the person who will live with the choice is the one making it.
assess_focus: Establish this before working the cascade. The same finding lands differently on a chief executive who can act on it and an analyst who cannot, and advice aimed at the wrong authority is wasted.

label: Winning Aspiration
summary: What winning means, for whom, and in whose eyes - the purpose the rest of the choices serve.
assess_focus: Look for a definition of winning that could be lost, not a financial target and not a slogan.

label: Where-to-Play
summary: The arena: which customers, which offerings, which geographies, which channels, which stages of the value chain - and, by necessity, which not.
assess_focus: A Where-to-Play that excludes nothing is not a choice. Probe the unstated arenas, especially channel and intermediate customers.

label: Customer & Promise
summary: The specific customer whose action the strategy is meant to compel, the insight into that customer's context, and the promise made to them.
assess_focus: Push from abstractions ('the market', 'users') to a named customer whose behaviour can be described and observed.

label: How-to-Win
summary: Within the chosen arena, the reason a customer chooses you over the alternatives, and the reason that reason holds up against competitors.
assess_focus: Test for a single coherent logic that resolves to lower cost or to differentiation, not a portfolio of unrelated initiatives.

label: Competition & Context
summary: Who else is trying to win in the same arena, what they can and will do in response, and what about the landscape makes winning possible at all.
assess_focus: A strategy with no competitor in the story is a plan. Ask what a rival would have to fail to do.

label: Capabilities
summary: The activities that must be done distinctively well, and must reinforce one another, for the How-to-Win to be real rather than aspirational.
assess_focus: Trace each claimed capability back to the How-to-Win it serves; unattached capabilities are wish lists.

label: Management Systems
summary: The systems, measures, routines and ownership that build the capabilities and keep the choices alive after the offsite ends.
assess_focus: Ask what would have to change on Monday. If nothing in the measures, budgets or meeting agendas changes, the strategy has no mechanism.

label: Coherence of the Whole
summary: Whether the choices reinforce one another end to end, read in both directions, rather than each being defensible on its own.
assess_focus: Test pairs, not boxes: does this Where-to-Play make this How-to-Win easier, and do these capabilities make sense only here?

label: Logic, Assumptions & Testing
summary: The strategy treated as a theory: what must be true for it to work, which of those things is least likely, and how that will be tested before betting the company.
assess_focus: This is where the highest-leverage questioning lives. Separate the logic from the evidence, then find the weakest link.

label: Adoption, Cascade & Adaptation
summary: Whether the people who make daily choices know the strategy, own their piece of it, and can tell when it needs to change.
assess_focus: Ask who else could state this strategy without the deck, and what evidence would make the team abandon it.
